newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentine soybean crop may hit 13.4 mln tns - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Argentine soybean crop may hit 13.4 mln tns - Safras.

text.p: Argentine soybean production could reach 13.4 million tonnes in 1996/97, up 5.9 percent from the 1995/96 record harvest of 12.65 million tonnes, said Brazilian consultants Safras e Mercado.
Planted area is seen growing 5.2 percent to 6.3 million hectares against 5.99 million the previous year.
Productivity is also forecast to rise, albeit at a more modest rate, taking into consideration the increase in production of soybeans as a second crop with wheat.
With normal weather conditions, yield should reach 2.154 kgs per hectare, 0.5 percent up from productivity of 2.143 kgs per hectares seen this year.
In general, the weather has so far been favorable, with soil moisture levels good in the Santa Fe, Buenos Aires and Entre Rios regions.
Only in Cordoba has there been more irregular rainfall. In the week ending November 28, it had practically not rained in Pampa Umido, a key producing area.
Plantings are overall between 35 and 40 percent completed, roughly in line with previous years, Safras said.
But for sowings to continue, new rains will be necessary throughout the producing region, it added.
Crushings in 1996/97 are expected to continue to grow after reaching record levels from the 1995/96 crop.
Crushings in the 1996/97 marketing year are currently put at 9.95 million tonnes, up 6.3 percent from the previous year.

Working on the basis of a 13.4 million tonne crop in 1996/97, crushings could reach 10.50 million tonnes, reflecting the financial advantages of crushing in Argentina as opposed to Brazil, Safras said.
Thanks to new investments, daily crushing capacity is now expected to reach 17,000 tonnes a day in 1997, involving companies such as Cargill, Indo/LPC, Dreyfus, Ceval, Pecom-Agra and Vicentin.

Soybean exports are forecast to reach 2.3 million tonnes in the 1997/98 commercial year, up 15 percent from 1996/97 but well below levels seen in 1994 and 1995 and restricted by the greater competitiveness of Brazilian soybeans.
Soymeal exports are also estimated to rise five percent to eight million tonnes and soyoil exports to 1.77 million tonnes, up 1.65 million from the current marketing year.
Safras e Mercado's supply/demand outlook for the 1997/98 marketing year is as follows. Quantities are in 1,000 tonnes and the year starts on April 1 and ends on March 31.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
